Etymology

/et-uh-MOL-uh-jee/ - the stress falls on MOL · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Etymology means the origin and historical development of a word.

Curious where 'ketchup' came from, Dario fell into an evening of etymology and surfaced somewhere in seventeenth-century fish sauce.

Worked Example

The museum label beside the loom gives the etymology of 'text': Latin texere, 'to weave,' so a text was first a woven thing. Visitors look from the shuttle to the label and back, watching an old craft hiding inside a modern word.

Etymology is a word's documented history — not its definition, and not a guess. Knowing that 'text' once meant weaving doesn't tell you what a text message is; it tells you where the word has been, and history like that must be traced through records, not invented because it sounds right.

How Etymology Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

word history

word history: the plain-English name for the same study

derivation

derivation: the traced path a word took to its present form

Antonyms

current usage

current usage: what a word means today, wherever it came from

guesswork

guesswork: an origin story invented because it sounds right

How Strong Is It? — definition → etymology → linguistics

definition vs. etymology

definition vs. etymology: A definition is a smaller thing than an etymology — it stops at what the word means today and asks nothing about the road there.

linguistics vs. etymology

linguistics vs. etymology: Linguistics goes further than etymology: it takes in whole languages — sounds, grammar, change — where etymology follows the trail of single words.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — etym-

Root — etym-: true, real (Greek etymos)

Root — -ology

Root — -ology: study, account (Greek logos, word, reasoning)

Put it together

Put it together: Etym- (true) + -ology (study) = the study of the true sense. Greek scholars believed a word's oldest form held its truest meaning — hunt the origin and you hold the truth. Modern etymology keeps the hunt and drops the mysticism: origins explain, but today's meaning rules.

Use the root in a new word: geology

Use the root in a new word: geology: Geology reads the canyon wall like a stacked library of ancient shorelines.

Root Check

Word Choice

academic

Etymology is the scholar's word; 'word history' says the same thing at the dinner table. Keep it distinct from definition — what a word means now — and never let a good origin story override the record: the field's whole point is documented descent, not appealing guesses.
